## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

Filter out basic variables (Di and Yi, excluding additional covariates) used for analysis at the moment and create a csv file. 
```{r}
# basic model only with di and yi related variables
df_basic_d_y <- df |>
  select(AGEGRP, LFACT, AGEIMM, Citizen, YRIM, IMMSTAT)

head(df_basic_d_y)
library(readr)

# write to a file called “df_basic_d_y.csv” in your working directory
write_csv(df_basic_d_y, "cen_2021_clean.csv")

```


subgroup of citizen (where, if AGEGRP>16 => treated)
```{r}
#subset of citizens
df_dy_citizen <- df_clean |> 
  filter(IMMSTAT==1) |>
  mutate(treatment=ifelse(AGEGRP>16,1,0))
```

subgroup of immigrants (where, if YRIM<2011 => treated)
```{r}
#subset of immigrants
df_dy_immg <- df_clean |> 
  filter(IMMSTAT==2) |>
  filter((YRIM>2011&AGEGRP>16) | AGEGRP<=16) |>
  mutate(treatment=0) |>
  mutate(Citizen=0)
```

combine the two subsets to one dataset
```{r}
# one dataset for both citizens and immigrants
df_dy_comb <- rbind(df_dy_citizen, df_dy_immg)
```
